access_level: Full arXiv HTML and ACL Anthology proceedings PDF were available; the paper-linked [project site](https://agentlaboratory.github.io/) and its linked [GitHub repository](https://github.com/SamuelSchmidgall/AgentLaboratory) were inspected at README/site level only.

The authors report an 84% expense decrease versus prior autonomous research methods, but their task is ML research rather than web-based business synthesis. The authors state that literature review failed in 60–80% of runs for the three tested backends, while also reporting whole-workflow subtask success rates above 92%; the definitions/context for these figures are unclear in the accessible report, so the phase figure should not be used without checking the detailed experimental tables. Their limitations section also reports occasional hallucinated experimental results and reliance on LLM reviewers. **Engineering inference:** Staged work and review checkpoints transfer; autonomous code execution, ML experiments and the headline cost reduction do not establish a need or benefit for Veda. [Paper, §§3–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.04227); [project page](https://agentlaboratory.github.io/); [repository](https://github.com/SamuelSchmidgall/AgentLaboratory). See paper-audit-P01-P14.md.

title: DeepTRACE — Auditing Deep Research AI Systems for Tracking Reliability Across Citations and Evidence
related_code_or_data: No direct DeepTRACE code/data artifact URL surfaced; the paper claims a dataset release and cites an earlier unrelated/uncertain project repository
package_claim: ICLR 2026; peer-reviewed; mechanism: statement decomposition; factual support/citation matrices; one-sidedness and overconfidence audit
access_level: Full 22-page ICLR 2026 conference PDF.

notes: **Access:** Full 22-page ICLR 2026 conference PDF. **Source reports:** DeepTRACE decomposes report text into statements and constructs citation and factual-support matrices, with eight metrics. Its benchmark uses 303 questions (168 debate, 135 expertise) across nine public search/research systems; most reported metrics use 2,727 system responses. The paper reports citation accuracy of 40–80% across systems and high unsupported-statement rates for some tested systems. The LLM judge’s scores correlate with two human annotators at Pearson r=0.72 for confidence on 100 answers and r=0.62 for 100 factual-support checks; authors say they interpret LLM-judge outputs descriptively, not as ground truth. **Code/data:** The paper says it releases the DeepTrace dataset but the inspected paper did not expose a direct artifact URL; it cites an earlier project repo, which is not necessarily DeepTRACE’s own release. **Engineering inference:** Adopt claim-to-source support matrices as an evaluation pattern, then validate with human review; system snapshots and LLM scoring are not Veda performance evidence. [Paper, PDF pp. 1–2, 4–8](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/file/ad08767706825033b99122332293033d-Paper-Conference.pdf). See paper-audit-P01-P14.md.

title: ALCE — Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations

decision_relevance: evaluation lead: citation support checker
notes: **Access:** Full 24-page ACL Anthology PDF. **Source reports:** ALCE evaluates cited long-form answers across fluency, correctness and citation quality, with citation recall for whether statements are fully supported and citation precision for irrelevant citations. The paper’s abstract reports that even the best tested models lack complete citation support on ELI5 half the time. The automatic support metric uses an NLI model; the reported agreement with human labels is substantial for citation recall (κ=0.698) and moderate for precision (κ=0.525), so this is an imperfect proxy. **Code/data:** Paper links [ALCE code and data](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/ALCE). **Engineering inference:** A good basis for statement-level citation checks and a local evaluation harness, but its datasets do not establish commercial-report quality. [Paper, PDF pp. 1, 4, 8–9](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.398.pdf). See paper-audit-P01-P14.md.

title: RARR — Researching and Revising What Language Models Say, Using Language Models
package_claim: ACL 2023; peer-reviewed; mechanism: post-generation searching, attribution, and unsupported-claim revision
access_level: Full 32-page ACL Anthology PDF and official repository README.
decision_relevance: evaluation lead: post-synthesis citation audit and correction
notes: **Access:** Full 32-page ACL Anthology PDF and official repository README. **Source reports:** RARR is a post-generation retrieval-and-revision method: find evidence for existing text, revise unsupported claims while preserving the original as much as possible, and produce an attribution report. The paper reports improved attribution and >90% original-intent preservation in its evaluation, and describes task/metric limits: attribution and preservation may trade off, self-evident statements can be penalized, and claim scope matters. **Code/data:** [RARR implementation and evaluation data](https://github.com/anthonywchen/RARR). The README describes query generation, web search, an agreement gate, editing and attribution; it also documents external search/model API dependencies and a dangerous “hallucinate evidence” test option that must not be used for factual attribution. **Engineering inference:** A distinct post-draft audit/repair step is useful; it cannot replace evidence-first collection, and repair should preserve a trace of original and edited claims. [Paper, PDF pp. 1, 7, 9–10](https://aclanthology.org/2023.acl-long.910.pdf); [repository README](https://github.com/anthonywchen/RARR). See paper-audit-P01-P14.md.

title: Conflicting Needles in a Haystack: How LLMs behave when faced with contradictory information
related_code_or_data: No dedicated study code/data URL surfaced in the reviewed paper
package_claim: EMNLP 2025; peer-reviewed; mechanism: controlled contradictions tests; finds sensitivity to repetition, order and surface forms, and inadequate uncertainty signaling
access_level: Full 16-page ACL Anthology PDF.
decision_relevance: evaluation lead: test true conflict vs repeated evidence and require uncertainty status
notes: **Access:** Full 16-page ACL Anthology PDF. **Source reports:** The authors embed three mutually exclusive fabricated “needles” in long documents and vary position, repetition, layout and domain relevance. Models usually choose one answer confidently rather than signal uncertainty, with biases toward repetition, recency and surface form. The authors explicitly state there is no correct answer in this setup; limitations include English-only open models up to 70B and fabricated conflicts in fixed Wikipedia-derived haystacks. **Code/data:** No dedicated code/data URL was found in the inspected paper; its references cite the generic Needle-in-a-Haystack repository, not a verified release of this study’s artifacts. **Engineering inference:** Use conflict ordering/repetition as a robustness test, but do not interpret this synthetic setup as a measured rate of real-world evidence-conflict failures. [Paper, PDF pp. 1–2, 9](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1742.pdf). See paper-audit-P01-P14.md.

title: DeepResearch Bench
package_claim: research benchmark, 2025; mechanism: 100 PhD-level questions across 22 fields; report-level rubrics and citation trustworthiness assessments
access_level: Full [arXiv HTML v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11763), [project site](https://deepresearch-bench.github.io/), and [author repository](https://github.com/Ayanami0730/deep_research_bench). The repository README and license metadata were inspected; code was not run.
decision_relevance: evaluation lead: general deep research benchmarking
notes: - **Access:** Full [arXiv HTML v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.11763), [project site](https://deepresearch-bench.github.io/), and [author repository](https://github.com/Ayanami0730/deep_research_bench). The repository README and license metadata were inspected; code was not run. - **Source finding:** Paper authors report 100 PhD-level tasks across 22 fields, evenly split between Chinese and English. Their topic mix is informed by 96,147 raw search-chatbot queries filtered to 44,019 queries. RACE uses reference reports and adaptive criteria for report quality; FACT extracts statement–URL pairs and uses retrieved page text plus an LLM judge to score citation support and effective citations. Authors report human-alignment studies, while noting task-scale/domain-selection limits and that human evaluation was limited to 50 tasks across four agents (600 reports). The FACT pipeline depends on an LLM judge and Jina page retrieval, so the reported measures are not purely deterministic. - **Code/data:** The repository reports Apache-2.0. Its reviewed pages did not expose a separate data license; dataset rights are therefore **unknown** here. README instructions require hosted-model and Jina credentials for evaluation; no calls were made. - **Reuse:** Useful evaluation pattern for report criteria plus citation support, but it is a benchmark, not proof that an LLM judge is adequate for Veda’s high-impact claims. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.

The paper reports current systems satisfy fewer than half the rubrics. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.

package_claim: arXiv preprint 2025; mechanism: expert-designed research questions, citation faithfulness/groundedness and open consulting tasks
access_level: Full [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16280), [author repository](https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/ResearcherBench), and its README were reviewed. The repository page contains code and data folders but no visible LICENSE file; an attempted direct LICENSE URL returned 404. No separate data license surfaced, so reuse terms are unknown.
decision_relevance: evaluation lead: evaluation on ambiguous research questions, with domain caveats
notes: - **Access:** Full [arXiv HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16280), [author repository](https://github.com/GAIR-NLP/ResearcherBench), and its README were reviewed. The repository page contains code and data folders but no visible LICENSE file; an attempted direct LICENSE URL returned 404. No separate data license surfaced, so reuse terms are unknown. - **Source finding:** Authors report 65 questions across 35 AI research subjects, split into technical details, literature review, and open consulting; evaluation combines expert insight rubrics with claim/citation verification. Their reported systems perform better on consulting than precision technical tasks. Authors identify AI-only domain scope, small task count, and black-box commercial systems as limitations. - **Code/data:** Public repository and “open-source” language in the paper do not substitute for a license grant. Do not reuse code or benchmark data without resolving the rights. - **Reuse:** Insight plus factual-grounding evaluation is relevant, but the domain and sample limitations prevent direct transfer of its comparative rankings to business research. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.

package_claim: BMJ 2021; established reporting guideline
access_level: Full peer-reviewed text of the same statement is accessible through the [PLOS Medicine open-access publication](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1003583) and official [PRISMA statement page](https://www.prisma-statement.org/prisma-2020-statement). The BMJ landing page/PDF in the CSV returned 403 in this browser; the PLOS publication is the co-published statement.
decision_relevance: methodology lead: transparent search, screening and inclusion flow
notes: - **Access:** Full peer-reviewed text of the same statement is accessible through the [PLOS Medicine open-access publication](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1003583) and official [PRISMA statement page](https://www.prisma-statement.org/prisma-2020-statement). The BMJ landing page/PDF in the CSV returned 403 in this browser; the PLOS publication is the co-published statement. - **Source finding:** The article presents a 27-item reporting checklist, expanded guidance, abstract checklist, and flow diagrams. Development included review of 60 guidance documents, a survey with 110 of 220 invited respondents, and a 21-member meeting. Crucially, the authors say PRISMA is primarily for reviews of health interventions and **is not** a guide to review conduct or a tool for judging methodological quality. - **Code/data:** Article is CC BY; checklists are available from the official PRISMA site. No software license is relevant to Veda. - **Reuse:** Adapt transparent reporting of search, screening, exclusions, and evidence flow; do not turn PRISMA into a numerical evidence-quality score. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.

title: GRADE Handbook
related_code_or_data: Not applicable; methodology handbook, not code or dataset
package_claim: established evidence-synthesis methodology; especially healthcare
access_level: Full [official handbook HTML](https://gdt.gradepro.org/app/handbook/handbook.html) was reviewed. The page says the handbook was updated in October 2013 and is being replaced by the GRADE Book, available since 2024.
decision_relevance: methodology lead: conceptually adapt risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias. Do not blindly transpose GRADE as a universal score for economics or consulting
notes: - **Access:** Full [official handbook HTML](https://gdt.gradepro.org/app/handbook/handbook.html) was reviewed. The page says the handbook was updated in October 2013 and is being replaced by the GRADE Book, available since 2024. - **Source finding:** The GRADE approach separates confidence/certainty in effect estimates from recommendation strength and discusses risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, and publication bias. The handbook explicitly targets health-care systematic review, HTA, and guideline audiences. - **Code/data:** Not applicable. This is guidance, not a released model or dataset. - **Reuse:** The evidence-domain vocabulary may inform an explicit confidence note. Applying GRADE as a score to business/market claims would be an engineering extrapolation, not a validated use of the handbook. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.

title: OpenAI Deep Research System Card

package_claim: 2025; vendor primary documentation, not independent evaluation
access_level: Full [official Deployment Safety Hub system-card HTML](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/deep-research), linked from the [OpenAI publication page](https://openai.com/index/deep-research-system-card/). Published 25 Feb 2025.
decision_relevance: security lead: prompt injection, privacy, browsing and safety threats. Treat product-owner benchmarks as descriptive rather than neutral comparative evidence
notes: - **Access:** Full [official Deployment Safety Hub system-card HTML](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/deep-research), linked from the [OpenAI publication page](https://openai.com/index/deep-research-system-card/). Published 25 Feb 2025. - **Source finding:** OpenAI describes an early o3 version optimized for browsing, its evaluation process, and risks including prompt injection, privacy, code execution, bias, and hallucination. The card reports mitigations but also residual prompt-injection risk and limitations in evaluation coverage. These are vendor-authored disclosures for the release described, not an independent comparison or current specification for every later system. - **Code/data:** No reusable code or benchmark dataset is presented by this source. - **Reuse:** Supports treating retrieved pages as untrusted input, constraining tool authority, and preserving privacy. Those are engineering implications, not proof that the documented mitigations transfer to Veda. See paper-audit-P15-P28.md.
